> I think this should be implemented as a new `binary_sensor` platform. 

If I understand this correctly, this would mean that there would be an additional **binary entity** that is not related to the existing **hot_water device**.  The existing *hot_water* device currently displays the current mode (_SCHEDULED,  MANUAL, OFF_).  I think the **binary** value should be integrated with the existing device.

> Have you been able to test this change? Because it looks like it would cause errors and only updates the state when you turn it on

Yes, I've tested this and it works without causing any errors.  It updates the new `current_state` attribute when the water heater switches on or off.  It doesn't affect the current `state` value, which reports the current operation **mode** (_SCHEDULED,  MANUAL, OFF_).   Changing this would be a breaking change.

> . . . . which doesn't seem to satisfy the requirement to show on/off state when the device is set to Schedule mode.

The original issue was raised by myself, and I am satisfied that it meets the requirements of: _'Hive Water Heater does not **report** the current operation'_.  I agree that it does not **show** on/off state, but that wasn't the requirement (though, that would be nice, and perhaps that could be a future enhancement based on my change?).

Actually, I've just managed display the `current_state` attribute value in the UI without any further work:

![water_heater](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/30695106/aadb68ee-ef0f-4c92-a819-86e11863004d)

Here's the yaml that I used:

`type: entity`
`entity: water_heater.kitchen`
`attribute: operation_state`

> > I think this should be implemented as a new `binary_sensor` platform.
> 
> If I understand this correctly, this would mean that there would be an additional **binary entity** that is not related to the existing **hot_water device**. The existing _hot_water_ device currently displays the current mode (_SCHEDULED, MANUAL, OFF_). I think the **binary** value should be integrated with the existing device.
> 

The `binary_sensor` would be associated with the same device because you'd use the same `DeviceInfo` identifiers. This is the standard way to build integrations, i.e. devices with multiple entities: https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/architecture/devices-and-services
> 

> The original issue was raised by myself, and I am satisfied that it meets the requirements of: _'Hive Water Heater does not **report** the current operation'_. I agree that it does not **show** on/off state, but that wasn't the requirement (though, that would be nice, and perhaps that could be a future enhancement based on my change?).

I actually misread the PR first time and thought you were setting the new state in the `async_turn_on` function so ignore my comment about that.

Nonetheless I think the correct way to achieve what you are trying to do is via the binary_sensor platform https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/hive/binary_sensor.py.  I think putting this in the `extra_state_attributes` might satisfy your own requirement but it doesn't really improve the integration for other users who might not know it's there at all.

I'm happy to help you get there if needs be.

I've updated the code, as you have suggested.

However, I'm happy to look at implementing this as a new `binary_sensor` if you think it is the proper way to satisfy this requirement.  If you could assist, that would be great.  Is there an existing implementation of the `binary_sensor` platform in other devices that I could use as a template?

I've seen the `binary_sensor.py` file, but can't see how this could be integrated into the water_heater device.

> 
> I've seen the `binary_sensor.py` file, but can't see how this could be integrated into the water_heater device.

You don't add the binary_sensor to the water_heater.  Instead you add the water_heater device to the binary sensor file.  So add `water_heater_devices = hive.session.deviceList.get("water_heater")` to `async_setup_entry` and create a new `HiveHotWaterBinarySensor` along the lines of the existing HiveBinarySensor but with an `async_update` to run `self._attrs_is_on = await self.hive.hotwater.getState(self.device)`

- the same device provides the **water heater** functionality

My PR implements the missing functionality in a way that is consistent with the existing approach. Thanks to everyone for their input.

I'll keep an eye out for the day that this integration is migrated to the multiple entity approach, at which point I'll remove my dodgy script (I won't hold my breath for this).

Thanks for the willingness to contribute.

issue_context.title: Hive Water Heater does not report the current operation (on/off)
issue_context.body:
### The problem

When the water heater automatically switches on/off according to the schedule, there is nothing in the attributes that reflects this.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.2.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

Hive

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/hive/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

I'm relatively new to the Hive integration, and have been using it for about two months now.  During this time, I believe that the attribute(s) has never reflected the current on/off operation state of the water heater, based on the timed schedules.

Is there a specific attribute ('current_operation') missing, perhaps?
